input.summary: Meridian's IT budget is run-heavy and change-light; seven strategic use cases lack funded, evidence-gated business cases.
covers: IT Budget Allocation — Run vs. Change

story.meaning: Meridian's IT spend is structurally weighted toward run-the-business obligations — Epic, on-prem infrastructure, SAS, and Tableau — leaving change-the-business investment thin and ungoverned against seven declared strategic use cases.
story.observed: 293 budget evidence references are loaded across run and change towers. No approved business case, signed baseline, or benefits ledger is evidenced for any of the seven value hypotheses. FY26 AI spend governance is listed as a use case, not a control — signaling the governance mechanism itself is unfunded.
story.matters: Without a funded, evidence-gated business case per use case, the board cannot distinguish strategic investment from discretionary spend. Every value hypothesis remains a hypothesis — not a commitment — and the CFO has no ledger to track realization.
story.supports: CEO, CFO, and CIO all cite AI/LLM automation, lakehouse, and call center optimization as top priorities. None have cleared the evidence gate required to move from planning to approved program funding.

findings: Run towers — Epic, on-prem SQL Server, SAS, Tableau, and legacy infrastructure — dominate the spend profile; change budget is thin relative to the seven declared strategic use cases.
FY26 AI spend governance is catalogued as a use case rather than an operating control, meaning no formal mechanism exists to gate, track, or rationalize AI investment across the portfolio.

All seven value hypotheses — lakehouse, AI/LLM, call center, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and automated close — lack approved business cases, signed baselines, and benefits ledger ties.
The CFO's AI Benefits Realization Ledger use case is itself in planning stage, creating a circular gap: the instrument needed to prove value is not yet funded or operational.

breakdown.title: IT Budget Posture by Tower — Meridian Health System

rows.label: Run: Applications (Epic, SAS, Tableau, Power BI)
rows.note: Dominates run budget; change investment constrained by these obligations

rows.label: Run: Infrastructure & On-Prem
rows.note: On-prem SQL Server and legacy estate; AWS/Databricks migration not yet funded to production

rows.label: Run: Managed Services & Cybersecurity
rows.note: OneTrust, Microsoft Purview, ServiceNow; AI governance controls not yet layered

rows.label: Change: Data & AI Programs
rows.note: Seven use cases in planning; no signed baseline or benefits ledger for any

rows.label: Change: AI Governance & Model Risk
rows.note: HITL, audit logging, and model-risk controls unfunded; CISO flagged as gap

chain: IT Budget allocation → funds (or starves) evidence-closure work for seven use cases
Evidence closure → gates business case approval for lakehouse, AI/LLM, call center, cost transparency, payment integrity, provider quality, automated close
Approved business case → enables CFO Benefits Realization Ledger to activate
Benefits Realization Ledger → provides board-grade proof of AI investment return
AI spend governance (FY26) → must shift from use case to operating control before any program funding is committed
relationships.note: Budget is the upstream constraint: until run-vs-change rebalancing is approved and evidence gates are funded, all seven strategic use cases remain in planning and the CFO has no ledger mechanism to track or defend AI investment to the board.

gaps.missing: No approved business case or signed baseline for any of the seven value hypotheses
gaps.blocks: CFO cannot commit to, track, or defend AI program spend; all use cases remain planning-grade
gaps.needed: FP&A-validated business cases with baseline owners, benefit categories, and realization milestones per use case
gaps.handoff: CFO / Finance & Value team to own baseline signoff; CIO to gate program funding release

gaps.missing: AI Benefits Realization Ledger is itself in planning — the tracking instrument is unfunded
gaps.blocks: No mechanism exists to reconcile AI spend against realized outcomes for board reporting
gaps.needed: Funded ledger design, system of record (Workday/ServiceNow), and CFO-owned reporting cadence
gaps.handoff: CFO to sponsor; CIO and CDAO to provide program and data inputs

gaps.missing: FY26 AI spend governance is a use case, not an operating control
gaps.blocks: No formal gate exists to approve, rationalize, or halt AI investments across the portfolio
gaps.needed: Governance framework with investment thresholds, evidence requirements, and CISO/model-risk sign-off criteria
gaps.handoff: CIO to own framework; CISO to own model-risk and audit-logging controls

gaps.missing: Run-vs-change budget split is not evidenced at a level sufficient for rebalancing decisions
gaps.blocks: Leadership cannot quantify how much run obligation constrains strategic change capacity
gaps.needed: Tower-level spend extract with run/change tagging, validated by FP&A
gaps.handoff: CIO and CFO to co-own tower taxonomy; FP&A to validate actuals vs. plan

gaps.missing: No HITL, audit logging, or model-risk budget line evidenced for any AI use case
gaps.blocks: CISO and compliance cannot certify AI controls; regulatory exposure unquantified
gaps.needed: Explicit budget allocation for AI governance controls tied to each use case program plan
gaps.handoff: CISO to define control requirements; CIO to fund within change budget

evidence.name: IT Budget Spend & Value Dataset
evidence.facts: 293 evidence references across run and change towers: applications, infrastructure, managed services, cybersecurity, data/AI programs, and AI governance. High confidence: 234 rows; medium: 64 rows. No realized-value claims are supported without tower evidence and FP&A validation.
evidence.fields: Tower, spend category (run/change), use case linkage, confidence, active/candidate status, value hypothesis, evidence ID
evidence.supports: Run tower dominance, change budget thinness, and absence of approved business cases across all seven use cases
evidence.missing: FP&A-validated actuals, approved business cases, signed baselines, benefits ledger ties, and PHI controls

evidence.name: Value Hypothesis Evidence Bundle (MER-V3-EVID-0360 to 0366)
evidence.type: Synthetic planning-grade evidence — seven use cases
evidence.facts: All seven use cases — lakehouse, AI/LLM, call center, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, automated close — are high or medium confidence but explicitly conditioned: value is quantifiable only after evidence gates are certified and baseline owners sign off.
evidence.fields: Use case name, value hypothesis, evidence gate conditions, confidence, active/candidate status
evidence.supports: No use case has cleared its evidence gate; none are decision-grade for budget commitment
evidence.missing: Baseline owner signoff, certified evidence gates, and FP&A-validated benefit quantification for all seven

evidence.name: Stakeholder Interview Evidence (MER-SA07-INT-EVID-0001 to 0033)
evidence.rows: 33 interview evidence records across CEO, CFO, CIO, CTO, CISO, Chief Experience Officer
evidence.facts: CEO, CFO, and CIO all cite AI/LLM automation, lakehouse, and call center optimization as top priorities. Every stakeholder signal is conditioned: 'promising but not decision-grade until evidence closes.' No stakeholder has approved a funded program.
evidence.fields: Stakeholder role, use case, confidence, blocking evidence gap, decision-grade status
evidence.supports: Executive alignment on priorities exists; funding commitment does not
evidence.missing: Approved program charters, budget allocations, and evidence gate closure confirmations from any stakeholder

evidence.name: Run Tower Evidence (BUD-RUN series)
evidence.type: Synthetic budget tower evidence — run category
evidence.rows: 29 run-tower evidence records across applications, infrastructure, managed services, cybersecurity, data, and workplace
evidence.facts: Run towers cover Epic, on-prem SQL Server, SAS, Tableau, Power BI, claims platform, pharmacy platform, CRM, and contact center telephony. These obligations are evidenced and structurally dominant in the budget profile.
evidence.fields: Tower, system, spend category, evidence ID
evidence.supports: Run spend is the primary budget constraint limiting change investment capacity
evidence.missing: Actual dollar amounts, FP&A-validated run totals, and run-reduction roadmap tied to cloud migration

evidence.name: Change Tower Evidence (BUD-CHG series)
evidence.type: Synthetic budget tower evidence — change category
evidence.rows: 36 change-tower evidence records across data, integration, cybersecurity, EHR, member, cloud, operating model, and AI governance
evidence.facts: Change towers span data/AI programs, cloud migration (AWS/Databricks direction), EHR modernization, member experience, integration, and AI governance. AI governance change budget (BUD-CHG-AIGOV) has only 4 evidence records — the thinnest of all change categories.
evidence.fields: Tower, program area, evidence ID, change category
evidence.supports: AI governance is the most underfunded change category relative to its risk exposure across all seven use cases
evidence.missing: Approved change program budgets, milestone-linked spend plans, and benefits realization tracking for each tower

evidence.name: FY26 AI Spend Governance Use Case Signal
evidence.facts: FY26 AI spend governance appears in the use case catalogue under CIO / Enterprise Technology. It is not evidenced as an operating control, governance framework, or funded program. Its presence as a use case — rather than a policy — signals the control mechanism itself is in planning.
evidence.fields: Use case name, owner, system linkage (M365 Copilot, ServiceNow, Workday, GitHub Copilot, Databricks, AWS)
evidence.supports: No formal AI investment gate exists; spend decisions are being made without a governing framework
evidence.missing: Governance framework document, investment threshold policy, CISO model-risk sign-off criteria, and board reporting cadence

visual_blocks.title: Meridian IT Budget — Use Case Funding Readiness Gate
visual_blocks.subtitle: All seven strategic use cases are in planning; none have cleared the evidence gate required for approved program funding.

rows.gate: Open — medallion arch + identity spine missing
Open — governance model + semantic layer missing
Open — transcript governance + intent taxonomy missing
Open — SAS lineage + entity resolution missing
Open — HEDIS/STAR attribution + contract linkage missing
Open — GL lineage + close workflow integration missing
Open — ledger design + system of record unfunded

data.decision_note: No use case advances to funded program status until its evidence gate closes, a baseline owner signs off, and FP&A validates the benefit quantification. The CFO's ledger must be funded first to make any other realization claim defensible.
